Thanks Maya — I reviewed Finex's asks and your redline. High-level comments:

1) 24 hours: We should avoid an absolute "initial notification within 24 hours of detection" for all events. Detection time can be unreliable (false positives). I recommend: 
   - Initial acknowledgement of receipt of an alert within 24 hours of discovery, and
   - Confirmed notification within 72 hours of confirmation that personal data was reasonably likely accessed/exfiltrated.

2) Scope language: Limit obligation to "Personal Data" as defined in DPA + systems reasonably dedicated to the customer's workload. Exclude platform telemetry and third-party maintenance events unless they affect customer personal data.

3) Subprocessors: Redwood will notify customers 'without undue delay' once we have reasonable evidence that a subprocessor incident affected personal data. For contractual clarity, let's propose a 48-hour window from Redwood's confirmation that a subprocessor caused an exposure to notify downstream customers. This is negotiable but gives customers a timely heads-up.

4) Evidence & transfers: We need to carve out time for forensics. Suggest: initial encrypted evidence package (redacted as needed) within 10 business days; full forensic report within 30 calendar days, with a good-faith commitment to update as more info emerges. We should also require Finex to sign an evidence transfer NDA/TOU when requesting raw logs.

5) Limitations & remedial actions: Add a clause allowing Redwood to redact unrelated customer data from evidence and to refuse transfers that violate privacy or export controls.

I attached a doc with suggested clause text (suggested_clauses.docx). If we take this to the customer, we should propose: acknowledgement within 24h, confirmation within 72h for confirmed personal-data incidents, detailed report in 7-30 days depending on severity, and evidence transfer under NDA.

Operational realities from infra/ops:

- Detection vs confirmation: We typically detect anomalous behavior within minutes-hours, but root cause analysis (to confirm personal data exposure) often takes days.
- Acknowledgement: We can commit to an initial acknowledgement to the customer within 24 hours of detection (even if only to say "we are investigating").
- Evidence handover: Secure S3 presigned links or an encrypted share are fine. Realistically we can stage an initial encrypted sample within 5 business days for triage, and a more complete forensic export within 14 business days depending on retention and re-ingestion needs.
- For subprocessor incidents: we can't unilaterally compel a subprocessor to transfer raw logs immediately; timelines should be conditional on subprocessor cooperation and applicable export laws.

Proposed operational text to align with legal:
- "Initial acknowledgement within 24 hours of detection; preliminary incident summary within 72 hours of confirmation; preliminary encrypted evidence package within 5 business days; comprehensive forensic report within 14 business days, subject to lawful constraints."

I'll attach our evidence-handling diagram to show the pipeline.

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. We've reviewed internally and propose the following compromise to balance Finex's need for speed with our operational and legal realities:

1) Acknowledgement vs confirmation:
   - Acknowledgement: Redwood will acknowledge receipt of a security event report to the Finex security contact within 24 hours of detection ("we are investigating").
   - Confirmation: Redwood will provide a confirmed notice within 72 hours when there is reasonable evidence personal data was accessed/exfiltrated. If confirmation cannot be completed within 72 hours, Redwood will provide interim status updates every 72 hours until confirmation.

2) Follow-up reporting & evidence:
   - Preliminary incident summary with affected systems and impact estimate within 72 hours of confirmation.
   - Encrypted preliminary evidence sample for triage within 5 business days of confirmation.
   - Comprehensive forensic report within 14 business days of confirmation, with good-faith updates thereafter as investigations progress.

3) Subprocessor coordination:
   - Redwood will notify Finex without undue delay once Redwood has reasonable evidence that a Redwood subprocessor materially affected Finex personal data. We propose a contractual clarity line: Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to notify within 48 hours of Redwood's confirmation that a subprocessor caused an exposure, subject to subprocessor cooperation and applicable law.

4) Evidence transfer safeguards:
   - Raw logs or full datasets will be provided only under an evidence-sharing NDA/TOU and subject to export controls and redaction for third-party personal data. Transfer mechanisms: presigned S3 links or encrypted archive; Finex to confirm preferred mechanism in writing.

5) Scope & limitations:
   - Obligations apply to Personal Data as defined in the DPA and to services/systems reasonably dedicated to Finex's workloads. Routine platform telemetry and peripheral maintenance events are excluded unless they impact Personal Data or materially affect availability.

If Finex is comfortable with this approach we can produce a clean DPA redline for signature; I've shared a DocuSign link for the updated DPA draft: https://www.docusign.com/FINEX-DPA-2027.

Would appreciate confirmation that this compromise is acceptable or specific counter-proposals (e.g., changing the 72h confirmation window to 48h) by EOD Monday so we can stay on Finex's procurement timeline.

Best regards,
